title: Succession Certificate
trustLine: Correct court process. Strong documentation. Financial asset claim support.
heroParagraphs: When a family member passes away without clear nomination, Will, probate or asset-transfer documents, banks, companies, depositories, insurers and financial institutions may refuse to release money or transfer securities. A Succession Certificate helps legal heirs establish authority before such institutions and claim specified debts and securities through a court-backed process.

At Estabizz Fintech, we assist families, legal heirs, nominees, NRIs, widows, children, parents, siblings, executors, beneficiaries and financial claimants with Succession Certificate, including heirship review, asset identification, petition drafting support, document checklist, court-fee valuation support, public notice coordination, objection handling, bank/share/FD claim support and advocate/counsel coordination.

blocks.text: Succession Certificate is a certificate granted by a competent court authorising the applicant to collect or realise the deceased person’s specified debts and securities.

It matters because banks, mutual fund houses, companies, depositories, insurers and other institutions often need legally reliable proof before releasing money or transferring financial assets where the account holder or asset holder has died.

This service is relevant for legal heirs, nominees, surviving spouse, children, parents, siblings, family members, NRIs, administrators, beneficiaries and claimants who need to claim bank deposits, fixed deposits, shares, debentures, securities, insurance proceeds, bonds, dividends, mutual fund units or other financial assets of a deceased person.
Succession Certificate is not a licence. It is a court-issued certificate used to claim specified debts and securities of a deceased person.
It is governed mainly by the Indian Succession Act, 1925, court procedure, applicable personal succession law and State court-fee law.

It is not required in every inheritance case, but it is commonly required when banks, companies or financial institutions ask for court authority before releasing money or securities, especially where there is no nominee, no Will, family dispute or unclear legal-heir position.
In simple terms…
Succession Certificate is a legal document issued by the court that allows the rightful heir or claimant to collect money and securities belonging to a deceased person.
It is mainly used for movable financial assets, not for directly transferring title of immovable property like land, house or flat.
From a compliance perspective…

Succession Certificate requires verification of death, legal heirs, relationship proof, jurisdiction, debts and securities, asset value, nominee status, objections from family members, court-fee requirement, public notice, evidence and final claim-release process.

From a risk perspective, wrong asset details, missing heirs, incorrect jurisdiction, incomplete family tree, inaccurate valuation or undisclosed objections can delay the petition and create complications before banks, companies and courts.

faqs.q: What is Succession Certificate?
faqs.a: Succession Certificate is a court-issued certificate authorising a person to collect or realise specified debts and securities of a deceased person.

faqs.q: Is Succession Certificate a licence?
faqs.a: No. It is not a licence. It is a court certificate for claiming debts and securities after death.

faqs.q: Which law applies to Succession Certificate?
faqs.a: The Indian Succession Act, 1925 is the main law. Personal succession law and State court-fee law may also apply.

faqs.q: Is Succession Certificate mandatory?
faqs.a: It is not mandatory in every case, but banks, companies or financial institutions may require it where nominee, Will or heirship documents are unclear.

faqs.q: Which court grants Succession Certificate?
faqs.a: The competent District Judge or civil court grants it based on the deceased person’s ordinary residence or asset location.

faqs.q: What assets are covered?
faqs.a: Bank balances, FDs, shares, bonds, debentures, securities, dividends, interest and other debts/securities may be covered.

faqs.q: Can Succession Certificate transfer immovable property?
faqs.a: Not by itself. Immovable property usually requires mutation, partition, release deed, probate, letters of administration or other succession/property process.

faqs.q: Can Succession Certificate be used for bank account?
faqs.a: Yes. It is commonly used where bank balance or fixed deposit of the deceased must be claimed.

faqs.q: Can it be used for shares?
faqs.a: Yes. It may support transmission of shares or securities, subject to company/depository/RTA requirements.

faqs.q: Can nominee claim without Succession Certificate?
faqs.a: Sometimes yes, depending on institution rules and asset type. If there is dispute or no clear nomination, certificate may be required.

faqs.q: Does nominee become owner automatically?
faqs.a: Not always. Nominee may receive the asset, but beneficial ownership can still be governed by succession law and heir rights.

faqs.q: What documents are required?
faqs.a: Death certificate, ID/address proof, relationship proof, family tree, asset details, bank/FD/share statements, heir details and affidavits are commonly required.

faqs.q: Is legal heir certificate same as Succession Certificate?
faqs.a: No. Legal heir certificate identifies heirs. Succession Certificate is a court certificate for claiming specified debts and securities.

faqs.q: What is difference between probate and Succession Certificate?
faqs.a: Probate validates a Will and executor authority. Succession Certificate is mainly for debts and securities.

faqs.q: What if there is a Will?
faqs.a: If a Will exists, probate or letters of administration may be more appropriate depending on asset, jurisdiction and institution requirement.

faqs.q: What if other legal heirs object?
faqs.a: The court may hear objections, examine evidence and decide whether certificate should be granted.

faqs.q: Can one heir apply alone?
faqs.a: One heir may apply, but details of all near relatives/heirs must generally be disclosed and notices may be issued.

faqs.q: Is NOC from other heirs required?
faqs.a: NOC is useful where heirs agree. If not available, court process and notices become more important.

faqs.q: Can NRI apply for Succession Certificate?
faqs.a: Yes. NRI applicants/heirs can proceed through proper documentation, POA, notarisation/apostille and advocate coordination.

faqs.q: What is court fee for Succession Certificate?
faqs.a: Court fee depends on asset value and State law. It should be checked before filing.

faqs.q: Can certificate be extended later?
faqs.a: Yes, it may be extended to additional debts/securities, subject to court process and additional fee where applicable.

faqs.q: Can Succession Certificate be revoked?
faqs.a: Yes. It may be revoked on grounds such as defective proceedings, fraud, false allegation or other statutory grounds.

faqs.q: How long does it take?
faqs.a: Timeline depends on documents, court registry, notice publication, objections, court calendar and State procedure. No timeline can be guaranteed.

faqs.q: What is the biggest mistake in succession certificate matters?
faqs.a: The biggest mistake is filing with incomplete heir details, wrong asset schedule, wrong jurisdiction or unclear valuation.

faqs.q: Can Estabizz handle complete Succession Certificate support?
faqs.a: Yes. Estabizz assists with requirement review, legal-heir mapping, asset schedule, document checklist, petition support, court coordination through advocate/counsel and post-certificate claim support.
